title: The Twelve must be humble and follow the First Presidency
setting: In 1837, many church members in Kirtland, including some apostles, turned against Joseph Smith’s leadership. Thomas B. Marsh, president of the Quorum of the Twelve, came from Far West, Missouri, in July to reconcile the quorum. He had also been troubled that some apostles planned missions abroad without consulting him. In June, Heber C. Kimball and Orson Hyde had left to preach in England. Joseph Smith dictated this revelation to Marsh at Kirtland on 23 July 1837.
summary: The revelation tells Thomas B. Marsh that his prayers and alms for the Twelve are heard. It says some things in his heart displeased the Lord, but his sins are forgiven because he humbled himself. He is to bear record to Gentiles and Jews and keep his home in Zion. It tells him to be humble, pray for the Twelve, and admonish them sharply. The Lord says he will heal them if they do not harden their hearts. The Twelve are told not to rebel against Joseph, who keeps the keys until the Lord comes. Marsh holds the keys of the kingdom for the Twelve abroad, under the First Presidency. It warns that judgment will begin at the Lord’s house and calls the Twelve to purify their hearts.

contextNote.title: Humility as the condition for leading
contextNote.text: Marsh led a quorum divided by dissent, and he had his own grievance. Verse 3 forgives him “inasmuch as thou hast abased thyself”. Verse 10 makes humility the way forward: “Be thou humble”. The promised result is that the Lord will “lead thee by the hand” and answer his prayers. Verse 15 gives the whole quorum the same warning: “Exalt not yourselves”. In this passage, humility means accepting direction through Joseph and the First Presidency, not acting alone.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 111–114 includes this revelation’s counsel on humility and unity among the Twelve. What do verses 11–13 ask Marsh to feel and do toward his struggling brethren?
reviewNote: Read all 34 verses. Official heading gives Kirtland, 23 July 1837, to Thomas B. Marsh amid dissent involving some apostles. JSP introduction read for Marsh’s concern over Parley P. Pratt’s England plans, his trip from Far West with David W. Patten and William Smith, and the Kimball–Hyde mission. Marsh wrote the original, which is lost. Sidney Rigdon and Hyrum Smith are named in v. 17. Fact-check 2026-10-12: no changes
